value: stable minus 2 minor versions, raised only in a minor release, declared as rust-version in Cargo.toml and tested in CI

no build backend or bundler crate; Cargo's own manifest is the entire declaration surface. Artifacts land in Cargo's default workspace-root target/ directory - target/debug/ for the dev and test profiles, target/release/ for release and bench, target/<name>/ for a user-defined profile, gaining a target/<triple>/<profile>/ level whenever --target is passed - relocatable by CARGO_TARGET_DIR, build.target-dir or --target-dir. Library target: exactly one, declared explicitly as [lib] with path src/lib.rs and Cargo's default crate name rs_launch_blueprint (the package name with dashes replaced by underscores); doctest is not set here and is R82's. Binary target: exactly one, declared explicitly as [[bin]] with path src/main.rs and name rslbp, a different string from the package name rs-launch-blueprint, so cargo install rs-launch-blueprint installs the command rslbp and integration tests resolve it through CARGO_BIN_EXE_rslbp; autobins = false so no src/bin/*.rs file becomes a second published command without a manifest edit; default-run unset while there is one binary; no build.rs and no build-orchestration crate. Packaged-file scope: an explicit [package] include allow-list - /src, /README.md, /LICENSE-MIT, /LICENSE-APACHE, /CHANGELOG.md - never exclude, the two being mutually exclusive; Cargo.toml and any license-file are included whatever include or exclude says, and a minimized Cargo.lock is likewise outside include/exclude selection - cargo package adds it, generating one when none is on disk - but not unconditionally: cargo package --exclude-lockfile omits it, an override cargo publish has no flag for and this template never passes. The optional web surface adds no target here: it is a Cargo feature per F017, and whether it also gets a second [[bin]] carrying required-features is R69's
